2 A student investigates the reaction of sodium hydrogencarbonate with dilute sulfuric acid.
This reaction produces carbon dioxide gas.
Procedure
The student:
Step 1 pours 50.0 cm of dilute sulfuric acid into a beaker
Step 2 adds one spatula of sodium hydrogencarbonate to the acid
Step 3 immediately starts a stop-watch
Step 4 stirs the mixture until it stops fizzing
Step 5 stops the stop-watch
Step 6 records in Table 2.1 this reaction time.
The student repeats the procedure four more times with the number of spatulas of
sodium hydrogencarbonate shown in Table 2.1.
